info.title: CleanTG Server Draft API
info.description: Design contract only; no running server. HTTPS with arbitrary user-selected base URL. Telegram user identity, device authorization and PIN edit scope are separate. Proposed lease TTL<=5000ms; server accounts union of issued intervals. WebSocket is the preferred real-time candidate as of 2026-10-13; docs/realtime.md records the pending native/auth PoC and message contract. This OpenAPI defines REST semantics, not WebSocket frames. The original SSE /v1/events proposal is deprecated. See docs for trust, accuracy and migration limits.

deviceToken.description: Own CleanTG access token bound to device JWK thumbprint; never a Telegram token.

enrollmentToken.description: Fresh limited identity proof for bootstrap/enroll/recovery, not normal API access.

dpopProof.name: DPoP
dpopProof.description: RFC9449 proof. Fresh jti, correct htm/htu/iat, ath for resource token and required nonce.

P256PublicJwk.description: Public JWK only. Private key fields are rejected.

AuthStartResponse.description: claimSecret is delivered only here over TLS and is never put in browserUrl. PKCE/state/nonce for Telegram are managed server-side.

AuthResult.description: Confirmed result includes a short DPoP-bound enrollment token, never Telegram tokens. Fresh proof required for bootstrap/enroll/recovery.

items.description: Parse decimal ID exactly; semantic validation requires 0 < id <= 9223372036854775807. Never decode through double.

Policy.description: IANA timezone must be validated against the server tz database. No peer titles. Policy edits preserve usedMs; timezone changes are scheduled after the current period.

Budget.description: usedMs is server-accounted union duration plus carry-in. remainingMs includes held future; do not subtract held twice. usedMs may exceed a newly reduced limit.

TokenSet.description: Secrets; never log/cache in plaintext. Refresh is rotating and bound to the same device key.

BootstrapResponse.description: Recovery code is shown once; short encrypted idempotent response recovery is required.

RecoveryCode.description: One-time display. Old recovery code is invalid after rotation; no usage reset.

DeviceSessionRequest.description: Create a server-fenced process session. Retires earlier device sessions for renew; old permits still expire/account conservatively. ClientBootId alone is not a trusted fence.

Lease.description: Immediate-use permit. Deadline = continuousMonotonicAtRequestStart + validForMs, not response receipt + TTL. Duplicate operation never extends expiry. Response with a retired session/revision/period or expired local deadline is discarded.

CarryInRequest.description: PIN-scoped explicit conservative migration, not ordinary usage sync. Backend tracks imported high-water. A known baseline is looked up in a server-issued sourceEpoch record from ModeChangeGrant; clients cannot submit an arbitrary baseline. Unknown/legacy epochs conservatively contribute the full not-yet-imported cumulative amount.

ModeChangeRequest.description: Current device stops selected viewing before request. Never send the new URL, old server tokens or PIN to another origin automatically.

ModeChangeGrant.description: Short device-bound authorization for atomic local mode change. Server persists sourceEpochId with the immutable baseline/current period so a later return imports only the local delta. Deadline uses continuous monotonic time from request start, not editable local wall clock. Save local policy, verifier, counter and marker before clearing old credentials; best-effort revoke old device afterwards. Grant alone cannot reset server policy or budget.

Event.description: Realtime change hint. Fetch snapshot after gaps/reconnect. Events carry no tokens, PIN or peer titles. This schema alone is not a WebSocket frame contract.

Problem.description: Do not echo secrets or request bodies. Snapshot is included only for an already authorized profile.

x-draft-notes: No runtime or deployment is implemented.
A future model/integration test must prove union/accounting invariants; schema validation does not.
Revocation/policy delivery to an unreachable honest client is bounded by existing lease TTL, not instantaneous.
Migration counter baselines require server-issued markers, not trusting an arbitrary number.
